text.p: SME - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said he did not consider Slovakia's exclusion from the first wave of NATO and European Union enlargement as a failure of his governemnt.
- Meciar said he had no intention of resigning.

- European Union Foreign Relations Comissioner, Hans Van den Broek said there were still "serious political discrepancies" in Slovakia that were an obstacle to starting accession talks with Bratislava.
- The Opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) said it would to use all its connections abroad to persuade the West that Slovakia should not be isolated from the European community.
- More citizens would vote to dismiss Premier Meciar than President Michal Kovac if a referendum on tne question had been held at the end of June, a public opinion poll said.
NARODNA OBRODA - President Kovac on Thursday blamed Meciar's government for Slovakia's exclusion from the first wave of NATO and EU expansion.
- Head of Slovakia's Employers' Association Michal Lach said he was confident Slovakia would soon be accepted to the EU.
- Slovakia is to begin privatisation of health care property worth some 2.9 billion crowns.
- Slovakia's trade deficit with Russia totalled 21.72 billion crowns in the first four months of this year. The shortfall is expected to widen further.
PRAVDA - President Kovac has called for the government to resign and added he would support early elections.
- The import surcharge is expected to bring around 8.4 billion crowns to the state budget this year.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovak companies do not expect exclusion from the first wave of EU enlargement to have a strong immediate effect on their business.
